subject: Cross-region traffic steering — customer action plan & post-incident steps
messages:
From: CloudNet Status <ops@cloudnet.com>
To: ops@acmetech.com; support@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2027 02:15:00 +0000
Subject: Network disruption impacting EU / APAC regions — routing degradation

Hello customers,

We are investigating an ongoing networking control-plane issue that began at 02:03 UTC affecting instances in eu-west-1 and ap-southeast-1. Symptoms: intermittent packet loss, elevated connection reset rates, and increased latency on API calls routed through those regions. Our engineers are performing rolling mitigations; temporary reroutes are in progress.

Impact window: 02:03 UTC — ongoing (we will update every 30 minutes).
Workaround: We recommend customers pin traffic to unaffected regions (e.g., us-east-1) or enable multi-region failover.

Status & updates: https://status.cloudnet.com/incidents/2027-08-09-network-flap

Regards,
CloudNet Operations

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Jessica Lin <jessica@acmetech.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2027 02:32:12 +0000
Subject: Re: Network disruption impacting EU / APAC regions — Redwood mitigation steps for Acme

Hi Jessica —

Thanks for the heads up (and sorry for the interruption). We see the same CloudNet notice and are treating this as a severity-2 for impacted customers that have cross-region traffic. I’ve pulled together a short, prioritized customer action plan so your engineers can stabilize traffic quickly:

1) Pin your requests to us-east-1 (temporary): use the regional endpoint https://api.us-east-1.redwood.ai or pass region=us-east in the header.
2) Lower DNS TTL for client-origin domain to 30s if you control DNS; that lets you flip routing quickly.
3) Enable Redwood graceful-fallback in your service config: set fallback_priority=[us-east-1,eu-west-1] and max_retries=2.
4) If you use signed webhook callbacks, add us-east-1 IP ranges listed in the attached checklist.

I’ve attached 'acme-reroute-checklist.pdf' with the exact API snippets and firewall IP ranges. Marissa is adding a small shell script with curl commands you can paste into your runbook.

We will also:
- Keep your account on an elevated monitoring channel until the root cause is resolved.
- Offer a one-time credit for any request failures if you submit a short incident claim (Rishi will own credits).

Please confirm when your team has pinned to us-east and I’ll loop in engineering for deeper follow-up and a postmortem draft.

— Irene
Irene Choi
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.ai | +1 415 555 0192

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jessica Lin <jessica@acmetech.com>
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2027 03:05:48 +0000
Subject: Re: Network disruption impacting EU / APAC regions — technical steps & quick commands

Jessica / team —

Quick engineer-oriented checklist (runnable commands):

# 1) Test connectivity to us-east regional endpoint
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" https://api.us-east-1.redwood.ai/v1/models -o /dev/null

# 2) Force region header in application (example Node.js)
fetch('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'Authorization': 'Bearer ' + KEY, 'x-redwood-region': 'us-east-1' },
  body: JSON.stringify(payload)
});

# 3) Temporary nginx route (if you proxy)
location /redwood/ {
  proxy_set_header X-Redwood-Region us-east-1;
  proxy_pass https://api.redwood.ai;
}

I attached 'reroute-commands.txt' with the above and a short iptables snippet for firewall teams. If you want, we can run a quick joint runbook session (20 minutes) — I’m available 03:30–05:00 UTC.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Jessica Lin <jessica@acmetech.com>
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2027 04:12:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Network disruption impacting EU / APAC regions — credits & SLA handling

Hi Jessica —

We’ll make this straightforward: if you have API requests that failed or were returned with 5xx during the incident window we will process a one-time usage credit against your August invoice. Please reply to this thread with a short summary (time ranges and approximate request counts) and I’ll convert that into a credit request to billing.

Separately, we are lifting the standard regional routing limit for Acme for the next 72 hours so you can pin to us-east without extra approval.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai

From: Jessica Lin <jessica@acmetech.com>
To: irene_choi@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2027 10:42:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Network disruption impacting EU / APAC regions — customer confirmation

Thanks, Irene / Marissa / Rishi —

We pinned all production traffic to us-east at 04:05 UTC and rolled the change to canary then to 100% by 04:25. We ran the curl checks and the responses look healthy. We will gather the request counts for the failure window and share a short summary by EOD for the credit.

Two asks:
1) Can you share a short postmortem timeline once RD has one? We need it for our internal stakeholders.
2) Please include the suggested DNS TTL change in the final playbook (we lowered it to 30s for now).

Appreciate the quick help —

Jessica Lin
Platform Lead, Acme Technologies
